title: Tactical code workbench — review notes and followups
content:
Context:
Quick dump from 2025-09 to 2026-02 reviews where I tried to be more tactical: bias toward small, safe edits that reduce cognitive load in the hot path (generation/runtime). These are notes to use when I jump into a PR mid-review or pair-review with someone.

Quick mental model (carpentry metaphor):
- Small chisels > giant saws. Prefer surgical changes that are easy to reason about.
- Visible screws > hidden glue. If something affects latency or batching, make it explicit in code + a comment.
- Measure before you sand: add microbenchmarks or a perf trace when touching serving hot paths.

Checklist (fast pass, <10min):
- Does the PR include a short: "why this change" at top of description? If not, ask for 2-sentence intent.
- Files touched: any change touching kv-cache, batching, or runner? -> escalate to deep pass.
- Surface area: does change add extra allocations per token? (strings, new vecs, cloning)
- Config/flags: are defaults backward-compatible? Is there a migration note?
- Tests: unit for logic + a small runtime smoke in CI (prefer ephemeral trace in integration).
- Logging/metrics: new failure path? add metric + SLI note.

Deeper pass areas (if PR touches serving runtime or orchestration):
- Kernel/trace coupling: any new code that could block the per-token loop? (sleep, mutex lock, heavy allocation)
- Batching semantics: verify batching key invariants (input size bucketization, timeout heuristics).
- Cache invalidation: explicit TTLs, edge-case empty-prefix hits.
- Error handling: prefer explicit error surfaces over swallowing; make retries idempotent.

Refactor idea bank (short sketches):
1) "prefix-normalizer" helper: small util to canonicalize request prefixes before indexing into KV cache (reduce duplicate entries). Start as single-file with tests.
2) lightweight batch-sampler: heuristic wrapper that simulates different batch formation under dev harness (no runtime change) to evaluate tail latency.
3) split-runner: decouple ip/transport parsing from token generation pipeline for clearer perf ownership and tracing.

Follow-ups & owners (deferred tasks):
- Add perf trace snippets to PR template (owner: Noel). Ticket: ENG-1582.
- Quick microbench for small-vec vs boxed-slice in token buffer (owner: Arjun).
- Create a one-pager for safe cache migrations (owner: me).

Unresolved questions to ask in review threads:
- Why this path uses cloning instead of borrowing? (sometimes ok for pinning; ask for comment)
- Does the change alter sequence-length distribution assumptions? If so, which tests cover long-run tails?
- Is there an escape hatch (config) for stepping back to the previous model variant when errors spike?

Room for experimentation (lab notes):
- Try sampling 10k requests offline, re-run batch formation with proposed heuristics and generate latency CDFs. If p99 increases by > 5% reject change or tune thresholds.
- When touching KV cache keys, log a diff of key frequency and collisions for 24h in staging.

Quick formatting/housekeeping rules I keep hitting reviewers on:
- Keep function length under ~80 lines in hotpath files. If it grows, split with clear names.
- Add docstring + one-line perf note for functions that could be called per-token.

Notes-to-self (todo before next review sprint):
- Build a tiny CLI that replays a PR diff vs main and outputs probable perf-impact hotspots (heuristic based on touched files, allocations, and known hotpath markers).
- Consolidate this doc into a 1-page "hotpath review rubric" for onboarding.

Slack links / quick refs: #eng-serving-runtime (perf threads), #infra-observability (tracing questions), PR template repo (see linked artifact).

Random observations from recent reviews: large diffs that touch many files usually hide the actual intent. Ask for an intent map or split into preparatory + functional change PRs.

End of dump. This is intentionally terse; use as a checklist and copy bits into PR comments.
